headline: A 2014 law removed the federal requirement that car dealers give new-vehicle buyers a written emissions-compliance certification and warranty notice.
what_it_does: The law amends the Clean Air Act to remove a requirement that dealers of new light-duty motor vehicles give the buyer a certification that the vehicle meets emission standards. The dropped requirement also covered a notice of warranty rights if the vehicle failed to meet those standards. The official summary does not describe any replacement requirement.

who_it_affects.group: Dealers of new light-duty motor vehicles
who_it_affects.how: They no longer have to provide buyers with the federal emissions-conformity certification and warranty notice under the Clean Air Act.

who_it_affects.group: People who buy new cars, light trucks, and similar vehicles from dealers
who_it_affects.how: They will no longer receive this federally required emissions certification and warranty-rights notice at the time of sale.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted June 9, 2014; the official summary does not list a separate effective date.
